nodes.text: (Verse 2) 'So the king commanded that the soothsayers and the magi and the sorcerers and the Chaldeans be called together, to tell the king his dreams. And when they had come, they stood before the king.' Those whom we [call] soothsayers (harioli), the others translated as *epaoidoi*, that is, enchanters. So enchanters seem to me to be those who accomplish their business with words; magi, those who philosophise about individual things; sorcerers (malefici), those who use blood and victims and often touch the bodies of the dead. Further, by 'Chaldeans' I think are meant *genethlialogoi* [casters of nativities], whom the common people call *mathematici* [astrologers]. But custom and common speech take magi to mean sorcerers; among their own people, however, they are regarded otherwise, because they are the philosophers of the Chaldeans, and the kings and princes of that nation do everything according to the knowledge of this art. Hence too at the birth of the Lord the Saviour they were the first to understand his rising, and coming to holy Bethlehem they worshipped the child, the star showing [the way] from above (Matt. 2).
